### Waters Corporation and Quest Diagnostics Help Close Cervical Cancer Screening Gap Bringing Nationwide Access to the Most Comprehensive FDA-Cleared At-Home HPV Screening Option


October 20, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s205.q4cdn.com/962852172/files/doc_news/Waters-Corporation-and-Quest-Diagnostics-Help-Close-Cervical-Cancer-Screening-Gap-Bringing-Nationwide-Access-to-the-Most-Comprehensiv-WEHL2.pdf)


- Expands access to most comprehensive FDA-approved HPV test and at-home self-collection option across Quest's national clinician, health plan, and consumer channels starting in 2027
- First and only FDA-approved HPV test that supports all ASCCP Enduring Risk-Based Management Guidelines by providing comprehensive extended genotyping
- Quest Diagnostics serves half of U.S. physicians and hospitals and one in three American adults each year


MILFORD, Mass. and SECAUCUS, N.J.


, Oct. 20, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- Quest Diagnostics (NYSE: DGX), a leader in diagnostic information services, and Waters Corporation (NYSE: WAT), a global life sciences and diagnostics leader, today announced a collaboration intended to broaden access to clinically appropriate at-home cervical cancer screening through the FDA-cleared Onclarity™ Self-Collection Kit.1,2,13


This collaboration is the first formed by Waters that will provide access to the Onclarity Self-Collection Kit through clinical, health plan, and consumer health channels, along with patient service centers, in the United States. Quest serves one in three American adults and one in two physicians and hospitals each year, and has a nationwide network of over 2,000 patient service centers. This marks a significant step forward in the fight against cervical cancer, positioning both companies at the forefront of closing the U.S. screening gap.


Cervical cancer is largely preventable with regular screening and early detection of human papillomavirus (HPV), the leading cause of cervical cancer, yet screening gaps persist, in part because of the sample collection process of traditional tests, which is often inaccessible and uncomfortable for patients.2-6 The Onclarity Self-Collection Kit used with the BD Onclarity™ HPV Assay delivers breakthrough innovation by offering at-home patient self-collection while simultaneously reporting an extended number of individual HPV genotypes to provide more comprehensive results.7,14


"In the U.S., there are over 24 million un- and under-screened individuals and approximately 14,000 new cases of cervical cancer each year," 8 said Jeff Andrews, M.D., FRCSC, Vice President of Medical Affairs, Waters Advanced Diagnostics, Waters Corporation. "By bringing together Waters' diagnostic innovation with Quest's national reach and capabilities, we have an opportunity to make a meaningful impact for these millions of individuals who remain at risk, advancing our shared goal of eliminating this highly preventable disease."


Beginning in 2027, Quest will drive expanded patient access to Waters' innovation through their broad clinician channel, their Gaps in Care channel serving health insurance plans, and their consumer-initiated testing channel,[questhealth.com](http://questhealth.com/) , all combined with access to their patient service center network.


"Many women struggle to participate in traditional cervical cancer screening methods, primarily due to geographic, socioeconomic, and logistical barriers," said board-certified OB/GYN Damian ("Pat") Alagia, M.D., Senior Medical Director, Women's & Reproductive Health, Quest Diagnostics. "We believe in making healthcare more proactive, personal, and connected for all patients, including through transformational options like at-home self-collection to help fill critical gaps in access to care."


With the new self-collection option, more patients will be able to collect their own sample in the comfort of their home using the Onclarity Self-Collection Kit, enabled by the BD Onclarity HPV Assay.7 Patients will then mail the sample back to Quest or drop it off at one of the approximately 2,000 Quest patient service centers nationwide. Quest's full-service laboratory will process samples, powered by the fully automated BD COR™ System, which uses advanced robotics to prepare, analyze, and report results while preserving specimen integrity and ensuring reliable, high-quality outcomes.9


Certain HPV genotypes, including types 16, 18, and 45, are associated with an increased risk of cervical cancer, making genotype-specific information important for patient management.10 As HPV vaccination has reduced infections from HPV types 16 and 18, other high-risk HPV strains now account for a growing share of cervical disease, particularly among younger, vaccinated populations.11 The Onclarity Self-Collection Kit is enabled by the BD Onclarity HPV Assay, the first and only FDA-approved HPV test that supports all of the American Society for Colposcopy and Cervical Pathology (ASCCP) Enduring Risk-Based Management Guidelines.7,10 Updated Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) guidelines identify high-risk HPV testing, whether clinician- or self-collected, as the preferred screening method for average-risk individuals ages 30 to 65.12 The BD Onclarity HPV Assay offers extended genotyping beyond HPV 16, 18, and 45 and individually identifies HPV types 16, 18, 31, 45, 51, and 52 along with three sets of strategically pooled results, regardless of collection method.7


Quest Diagnostics is a leader in women's and reproductive health and offers a complete menu of solutions for screening and diagnosing cervical cancer. For more information, visit[www.QuestWomensHealth.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4801665-1&h=61489927&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.questwomenshealth.com%2F&a=www.QuestWomensHealth.com) .


Waters Corporation is an advanced diagnostics leader, offering the[FDA-cleared Onclarity HPV Self-Collection Kit for at-home use, used with the BD Onclarity HPV Assay with extended genotyping](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4801665-1&h=2128969911&u=https%3A%2F%2Fir.waters.com%2FNews--Events%2Fnewsroom%2Fnews-details%2F2026%2FWaters-Announces-FDA-Clearance-of-the-Most-Comprehensive-At-Home-Cervical-Cancer-Screening-Tool-the-Onclarity-HPV-Self-Collection-Kit-and-FDA-Approved-HPV-Assay%2Fdefault.aspx&a=FDA-cleared+Onclarity+HPV+Self-Collection+Kit+for+at-home+use%2C+used+with+the+BD+Onclarity+HPV+Assay+with+extended+genotyping) , marking a significant milestone in expanding access to cervical cancer screening and removing barriers that currently prevent many individuals from receiving routine screening.
